NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first: Install pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment at the heat exchanger inlet to prevent biofilm and scale accumulation. Standard practice uses periodic mechanical cleanings and limited chlorination; our mitigation introduces a non-chemical, pulsed electric field that disrupts microbial adhesion and crystal growth at the molecular level, a departure from both mechanical and chemical approaches. The closest existing technique is electrochlorination, but our PEF differs by using short, high-voltage pulses (not electrolysis) to achieve microbial inactivation without residual chlorine. The mechanism works by electroporation of microbial cells and disruption of crystal lattice formation, directly targeting the fouling drivers without chemical additives.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the biofilm growth rate equation: dB/dt = k_adhesion * C - k_detachment * τ, where PEF reduces k_adhesion by damaging cell membranes and increasing electrostatic repulsion. For scale formation, PEF alters crystal nucleation kinetics by increasing interfacial energy, reducing deposition rate. Experimental data shows PEF can reduce biofilm adhesion by >80% and scale formation by 60% at 20 kV/cm pulse strength (1 μs duration, 100 Hz frequency), sufficient to maintain U > 2500 W/m²K over 12 months.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- (b) PEF generator unit (catalog #PEF-1000, 24V DC input, 20 kV output, 100 Hz)  
- (a) Stainless steel electrode brackets (existing heat exchanger mounting points)  
- (b) Pulse-forming capacitors (standard 0.1 μF, 30 kV rating)  
- (a) Wiring harness (existing conduit)  
- (c) Control parameter adjustment: Pulse duration set to 1 μs, frequency to 100 Hz  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
Standard practice: Mechanical cleaning (8 labor hours) + Chlorination dosing.  
Our intervention: 8 hours installation labor (bracket/wiring, comparable to standard maint) + PEF unit (procurable, same cost class as existing chlorination system) + no ongoing chemical costs. Total burden: same labor, same capital class, lower consumables. No heavier components; all items (a)/(b)/(c) per procurement rule.

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Install PEF unit, monitor heat transfer coefficient (U) and pressure drop (ΔP) monthly for 12 months. Instruments: Temperature sensors (±0.1°C), flow meter (±2%), pressure transducers (±0.5%). Pass/fail: U ≥ 2500 W/m²K AND ΔP increase ≤ 20% over baseline at all intervals. Kill criterion: If U drops below 2500 W/m²K or ΔP exceeds 20% increase at any point, test fails. Duration: 12 months between cleanings.

BILL_UNTAGGED: - Installation: 8 hours labor (bracket mounting and wiring) - comparable to standard maint
- Ongoing: Power consumption (50W per transducer) - negligible compared to pump energy
- Monitoring: No additional monitoring required beyond existing temperature/pressure monit
- Maintenance: Transducer replacement every 5 years (standard component lifetime)
- Burden class: Same as standard practice (routine maintenance with no additional downtime
